scenario: Hinglish (Hindi in Roman script mixed with English): two days of loose motions and stomach pain; stomach infection; ORS and zinc.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Doctor sahab, mujhe do din se loose motion ho rahe hain aur pet mein dard bhi hai.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Ulti ya bukhar hai kya? Potty mein khoon to nahi aaya?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Ulti nahi hui, bukhar bhi nahi hai. Khoon nahi aaya, bas paani jaisa aata hai.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Haan, parso raat ko bahar chaat khayi thi, shayad wahin se hua. Pakka nahi pata.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Koi dawai li hai abhi tak?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Haan, ek goli li thi, loperamide, dukaan se. Aur mujhe thyroid hai, roz subah thyronorm leta hoon.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Theek hai. Pulse 96 hai aur BP 110 by 70 hai. Pet mein neeche halka dard hai, par pet naram hai. Zubaan thodi sookhi hai.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Doctor sahab, kahin typhoid to nahi hai? Office mein ek dost ko hua tha.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Nahi, lagta hai ye bas pet ka infection hai, shayad food poisoning. Paani ki kami bhi thodi hai.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Doctor sahab, aaj India ka match hai, par is haalat mein kaun dekhega.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: ORS ke packet paani mein ghol kar din bhar piyiye. Zinc 20 milligram din mein ek baar paanch din tak. Halka khana khaiye, jaise khichdi aur dahi. Aur stool test bhi kara lijiye.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Theek hai, phir kab aana hai?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Do din baad aaiye, ya pehle aa jaiye agar chakkar aaye ya pishaab kam ho.

notes: Code-mixed Hindi and English in Roman script (Hinglish), text only (no audio); spelling is informal and not standardised, as in real typed or transcribed Hinglish. An English-rule extractor is not expected to handle this file; it exists to measure behaviour on an unsupported language, including the partially English tokens (loose motion, thyroid, food poisoning, stool test, ORS, zinc) that a naive English matcher might pick up. Turn 5 (the street food remark) is an ambiguous cause and is unlabelled; turn 13 (cricket match) is small talk. The doctor's assessment in turn 12 is hedged (lagta hai, shayad).
